paper_metadata.title: Time-domain-multiplexed Gaussian Boson sampling for graph problems in finance

summary: The paper presents time-domain-multiplexed Gaussian Boson Sampling for four financial graph tasks: community detection, dense subgraph detection, clique finding, and AML subgraph isomorphism matching. The best reported simulation result is 0.9908 fidelity for fitting a 20x20 target unitary with a 4-mode, 10-timestep TDM circuit, and the clique benchmark identifies 7 six-node cliques in a 20-node graph.

experiments.description: Time-domain-multiplexed Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS) co-design for financial graph problems, including community detection, synthetic identity fraud dense-subgraph detection, collusive stock manipulation clique finding, and AML isomorphic subgraph matching, validated via numerical simulation and a 20-node unitary-fitting benchmark.

algorithm.variant: Gaussian Boson Sampling with time-domain-multiplexed photonic circuit co-design
algorithm.convergence_criteria: best fidelity over 8 rounds of batched optimization; 350 epochs per round
algorithm.parameter_initialization: randomly initialized circuit parameters; 640 optimization instances total (8 rounds × 80 configurations)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Adjacency matrix of each graph is mapped to a GBS device via Takagi-Autonne decomposition; target unitary U derived from graph adjacency matrix A. For subgraph tasks, k-photon post-selection over k-node subgraphs is used.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize GBS sampling probability / Hafnian-based signature correlation for dense subgraph, clique, and isomorphic subgraph identification; for unitary fitting, maximize fidelity between target unitary U and fitted unitary U_fit.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection on fixed photon number k for k-node subgraphs; auxiliary nodes added for isomorphic subgraph matching when needed

problem_instance.description: Four financial graph analytics tasks: community detection, synthetic identity fraud detection, collusive stock manipulation detection, and AML subgraph isomorphism matching; plus a 20-node collusive stock manipulation graph used for unitary fitting and clique finding.
problem_instance.dataset_name: synthetic financial graphs; Hidden dataset; AMLSim-derived banking transaction dataset

dataset_specification.description: Community graph synthetically generated; synthetic identity graph from ref. 27; collusive stock manipulation graph synthetically generated; AML graph from AMLSim with 8,000 nodes for the illustrative subgraph

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Transaction data converted to graph adjacency matrices; for AML isomorphism, auxiliary nodes are added to pattern and target graphs when needed; for GBS simulation, states with si in {0,1} and total photon number exactly k are post-selected
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical simulations in DeepQuantum; unitary-fitting benchmark reports best fidelity across 640 optimization instances; GBS output distributions compared between ideal spatial and TDM circuits; robustness evaluated under optical loss for 36×36, 64×64, and 100×100 matrices averaged over 10 random unitary matrices

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Graph construction from transaction data; Takagi-Autonne decomposition to map adjacency matrix to target unitary; sliding-window search for best embedded submatrix
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Identify dense subgraphs / cliques / isomorphic subgraphs from high-probability GBS outputs; compare Hafnian-based signatures for AML matching

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic reduction in hardware complexity; O(sqrt(N)) width and O(sqrt(N)) depth
speedup_claims.baseline_method: purely spatial Clements architecture / universal multiport interferometers
speedup_claims.conditions: for the proposed non-universal spatial-temporal hybrid photonic architecture
speedup_claims.caveats: Achieved by sacrificing universality; intended for problem-specific graph encoding rather than arbitrary unitary synthesis.

speedup_claims.conditions: 4-mode TDM circuit with 10 timesteps on a 20x20 unitary benchmark
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a simulation result, not a hardware demonstration.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(sqrt(N)) width and O(sqrt(N)) depth for the proposed hybrid TDM architecture

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: A photonic GBS circuit with a 4-mode time-domain-multiplexed architecture and 10 timesteps; benchmarked by numerical simulation on a 20-node clique-finding / 20x20 unitary-fitting task.
limiting_factors: Reported gain is hardware-complexity reduction, not proven computational advantage

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because all results are numerical simulations in DeepQuantum and no real QPU is used
num_qubits is not explicitly stated as qubits; the paper reports photonic modes / timesteps and global mode counts rather than qubit registers
speedup_order inferred as none_proven because the paper discusses scalability/hardware reduction but does not establish an asymptotic quantum speedup over classical algorithms
The paper emphasizes scalability and fidelity of a TDM photonic architecture, but does not demonstrate quantum advantage over classical methods.
